name: Slack
description: A Slack channel's live transcript, plus PIN-protected sending as this location

Slack account.help: Create a Slack app in the workspace (api.slack.com/apps → Create New App → From scratch) and, under OAuth & Permissions → User Token Scopes, add channels:history, channels:read, groups:history, groups:read, chat:write and users:read (users:read.email is not needed). Sign in to Slack as this location's account — the one named for the campus — open the app's OAuth & Permissions page and press Install to Workspace (or Reinstall to Workspace), then copy the User OAuth Token (xoxp-…) it shows and paste it here: messages from this machine are then literally from the location. A bot token (xoxb-…) works too; it posts as the app, with "Send as" naming the location.

Sending.help: Messages leave this machine only from a Send or Quick replies tile, and only after the PIN is entered on that tile — every tile asks again after Auto-lock minutes without a send. Sending stays refused until a 4–8 digit PIN is set here. Quick replies are one per line, Label | Message, with an optional | #channel-name to send that one somewhere other than the transcript channel.

token.label: Token
token.help: The location account's User OAuth Token (xoxp-…, recommended) or a Bot User OAuth Token (xoxb-…).

sendAs.label: Send as
sendAs.help: Only used with a bot token — a user token always sends as its own account; needs the chat:write.customize scope.

channel.label: Channel
channel.help: The channel the transcript shows and messages go to by default. Only channels the account has joined are listed — join one in Slack first.

pollSeconds.label: Refresh interval (s)
pollSeconds.help: How often the channel is re-read (1 s at the fastest).

pin.label: PIN
pin.help: 4–8 digits; asked every time a send tile opens.

quickReplies.label: Quick replies
quickReplies.help: One per line: Label | Message. Add | #channel-name to send one somewhere else.
